page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg7.12xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8369HB processor running at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz, providing 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 192.0 GB of RAM, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per physical core. It operates on the KVM hypervisor and includes dedicated CPU allocation. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, and it lacks GPU acceleration. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 16 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the ecs.hfg7.12xlarge in the average tier for most compute and memory tasks, with some notable exceptions. The instance achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1578.39 and a multi-core score of 49936.52. Its memory subsystem demonstrates strong performance in specific workloads, as evidenced by a PassMark memory score of 2786.2, which ranks in the top 25 percent. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is also a strong point, reaching 206.4 GB/sec. However, large-block uncached memory read and write speeds are moderate at 127.79 GB/sec and 53.45 GB/sec, respectively. Redis SET operations perform at an average rate of 40.87 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput reaches 26.83 GB/sec.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.hfg7.12xlarge is the complete absence of local storage, requiring reliance on network-attached storage for persistent data. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a high density of dedicated Intel Xeon compute resources paired with a balanced memory allocation, making it suitable for workloads that require consistent CPU performance without the premium of GPU hardware. Appropriate workloads include multi-threaded data decompression, software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and general-purpose enterprise applications that do not require local NVMe storage.
